plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack) based on prior iteration evidence. Iteration_06 achieved best_target_score 0.647, while iteration_16 regressed to 0.433. Feedback directives specify initializing from iteration_16's best thickness vector with ±8% perturbation and enforcing a 45 nm maximum adjacent-layer thickness difference to prevent spectral oscillations from abrupt transitions. Three complementary routes are proposed: (1) bounded perturbation refinement with smoothness constraint, (2) alternative SiO2/HfO2 material pair to test index-contrast sensitivity, (3) increased 24-layer count to explore whether additional degrees of freedom improve the 0.647 ceiling. All routes preserve the 20-layer or 24-layer alternating topology, fused silica substrate, air incidence, and three-band transmittance objectives. Parent_route_id is set to 'route_02' per refinement_chain instruction.

routes.title: Bounded perturbation MgF2/HfO2 stack with adjacent-layer smoothness constraint
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing optimization from iteration_16's best thickness vector [33.0, 74.0, 101.0, 34.0, 109.0, 53.0, 21.0, 12.0, 114.0, 26.0, 74.0, 43.0, 52.0, 59.0, 138.0, 16.0, 22.0, 71.0, 190.0, 67.0] with ±8% perturbation bounds and enforcing maximum 45 nm thickness difference between adjacent layers will reduce spectral oscillations and improve best_target_score above the iteration_16 value of 0.433, potentially recovering toward the iteration_06 peak of 0.647.
routes.design_principle: Smooth thickness gradients prevent high-frequency spectral ripple caused by abrupt optical thickness transitions. Bounded perturbation around a known good candidate focuses search on local refinements rather than global re-exploration.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: Air | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Exact layer count: 20 finite layers (10 MgF2, 10 HfO2).
design_variables: layer thicknesses (20 variables, bounded ±8% around iteration_16 best candidate)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm passband
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: adjacent layer thickness difference ≤ 45 nm for deposition uniformity
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer response
Quarter-wave stack principle for stopband formation
Smooth thickness gradients reduce spectral ripple
expected_advantages: Focused search around known good candidate reduces optimization iterations
Smoothness constraint prevents non-manufacturable abrupt transitions
May recover iteration_06 performance while maintaining iteration_16 structural insights
known_risks: ±8% bounds may be too restrictive to escape local optimum
Smoothness constraint may prevent optimal chirp profiles
MgF2/HfO2 material pair may have intrinsic limitations below 0.647 score ceiling
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating MgF2 and HfO2 layers starting with MgF2 (20 finite layers total: 10 MgF2, 10 HfO2). Initialize thicknesses at [33.0, 74.0, 101.0, 34.0, 109.0, 53.0, 21.0, 12.0, 114.0, 26.0, 74.0, 43.0, 52.0, 59.0, 138.0, 16.0, 22.0, 71.0, 190.0, 67.0] nm. Apply thickness bounds of ±8% around initialization values. Enforce constraint that absolute difference between adjacent layer thicknesses must not exceed 45 nm. Use coherent S-matrix solver across 255-1100 nm wavelength range at normal incidence. Score three mean-transmittance objectives: maximize in 255-280 nm, minimize in 300-700 nm, minimize in 700-1100 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with bound projection. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Iteration_16 showed score regression to 0.433 from iteration_06's 0.647. Feedback directives specify initializing from iteration_16 best thickness vector with ±8% perturbation and 45 nm adjacent-layer smoothness constraint to prevent spectral oscillations from abrupt transitions.

routes.title: SiO2/HfO2 alternative material pair with 20-layer alternating topology
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing MgF2 with SiO2 as the low-index material while retaining HfO2 as high-index will change the refractive index contrast and dispersion characteristics, potentially enabling better passband transmission and stopband rejection if MgF2 absorption or index mismatch limits performance in the 255-280 nm region.
routes.design_principle: Material pair selection determines index contrast, which controls stopband width and reflectivity. SiO2 has lower UV absorption than MgF2 below 200 nm but comparable transparency in 255-280 nm range. Testing alternative pairs isolates material-limited vs. topology-limited performance.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: Air | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Exact layer count: 20 finite layers (10 SiO2, 10 HfO2).
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm passband
minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: SiO2 and HfO2 both compatible with ion-assisted deposition
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer response
Index contrast determines stopband width in periodic stacks
Material absorption edges affect UV transparency
expected_advantages: SiO2 may have lower UV absorption than MgF2 in 255-280 nm range
Higher index contrast (SiO2 n~1.46 vs MgF2 n~1.38 at UV) may widen stopbands
Tests whether MgF2/HfO2 pair is intrinsically limited
known_risks: SiO2 refractive index dispersion may shift stopband positions
SiO2/HfO2 stress mismatch may affect film stability
May not improve over MgF2/HfO2 if topology rather than materials limits performance

routes.title: 24-layer MgF2/HfO2 stack to test degrees-of-freedom hypothesis
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 24 layers provides additional degrees of freedom for the optimizer to shape the spectral response, potentially enabling better simultaneous optimization of passband transmission and dual stopband rejection if 20 layers are insufficient to satisfy all three objectives.
routes.design_principle: More layers provide more interference conditions to manipulate, enabling finer spectral control. However, diminishing returns occur beyond a certain layer count, and manufacturing complexity increases. Testing 24 layers (still under 30-layer limit) explores whether the 0.647 score ceiling is layer-count-limited.
